key_concepts: Magma is molten rock beneath Earth's surface; lava is molten rock erupted onto the surface
Magma and lava are extremely hot silicate-rich mixtures that may contain gases and solids.
Earth's interior layers can be compared to a hard-boiled egg: crust, mantle, and core.
Volcanoes are classified as active or inactive based on eruption history.
Active volcanoes have records of eruption within the last 600 years or 10,000 years ago.
Inactive volcanoes have not erupted for the last 10,000 years and show weathering and eros
Basaltic magma is low in silica, fluid, and produces quiet, nonexplosive eruptions.
Silica-rich granitic magma is thick, traps gas, builds pressure, and produces explosive er

Volcano cone shapes include cinder, composite, and shield, and relate to magma composition
Latitude and longitude are used to locate volcanoes on maps.
